examples.title: Residential Time-of-Use (Electric Home) Service
examples.description: This optional schedule applies to individually-metered electric service to residential customers who have one or more of the following qualifying electric technologies: Electric vehicle charging; Energy storage; or Electric heat pump for water heating or climate control.

examples.title: Residential Time-of-Use (Electric Home) Service — Smart Meter / Tiered
examples.description: Variant of E-ELEC requiring an AMI smart meter at the service point, with a 2,000 kWh monthly consumption eligibility limit and two service tiers (Baseline 0–500 kWh, Over-Baseline 500–2,000 kWh). Demonstrates ServicePointProfile, consumption-based eligibility Conditions, and ServiceTier structures.

examples.title: Residential Real-Time Pricing (RRTP)
examples.description: ComEd's Residential Real-Time Pricing program where hourly supply prices are based on PJM day-ahead LMP plus a retail adder. Demonstrates DynamicPricing with realTimePricing type, PriceUpdateRule for wholesale market integration, seasonal structure, and a full billing model with supply, delivery, service, and adjustment ledgers.

examples.title: Small General TOU with Peak Day Pricing (B-6 PDP)
examples.description: PG&E's small general service time-of-use rate with a Peak Day Pricing overlay. On PDP event days (up to 15 per year), peak period prices (14:00–18:00) are replaced with a critical peak adder. Demonstrates DynamicPricing with criticalPeakPricing type, TOUSchedule with peak/off-peak tiers, demand charges, and event-triggered PriceUpdateRule driven by CAISO grid conditions.
